newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to issue new unlinked bond on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Israel to issue new unlinked bond on Wednesday.

text.p: Israel on Wednesday will issue 100 million shekels worth of a new unlinked bond yielding 16.7 percent, a Finance Ministry spokesman said on Sunday.

The bond will be a three-year version of the existing Shahar bond currently issued for one and two years. The principal and interest of the Shahar are unlinked and the bond is issued at a fixed annual interest rate determined by the Finance Ministry. Interest is paid once a year.

The spokesman said the ministry will also issue on Wednesday 150 million shekels worth of two-year Shahar bonds, 105 million shekels worth of the seven-year Kfir, which is linked to the consumer price index (CPI), 150 million shekels worth of the four-year unlinked Gilon and 50 million shekels worth of the dollar-linked Gilboa.
Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments said he believes the new Shahar bond will be snapped up by investors because the yield offered is high and the investment is attractive.
Commenting on the other bonds to be issued on Wednesday, Halpern said it is clear the government prefers to issue short-term bonds and not long-term CPI-linked bonds whose yields are high.

Prices of long-term CPI-linked bonds took a battering recently and saw yields soaring after provident funds, long-term savings funds with special tax benefits, dumped them to meet massive public redemptions.
